clue.text: Fast, about to be chasing good whisky

indicators.note: the fast-and-life piece comes after, chasing, the letter for good
the word for a fast goes round, about, the verb for existing

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A drinker hurries to grab a good malt before it is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for speed, but it is the noun, the Christian season of fasting, with 'about' putting the verb for existing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenlivet is a well-known Speyside single malt, a specific example of Scotch.

clue.text: Feed abrasively?

parts.note: one word means both to eat grass in a field, as cattle do, and to scrape the skin lightly

explanation.definitionFit: Animals feeding on pasture do this, and a scraped knee is the same word, hence the abrasive feeding.

clue.text: Former paying guest partly retained by headless parson to bowdlerise

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
PG, a paying guest, is split: one letter goes before and only part is held inside

indicators.note: held inside, so the second letter sits within the clipped clergyman
the parson's word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a curate is a junior parish clergyman
the other letter of PG, the abbreviation for paying guest

explanation.surface: A former lodger is kept on by a clergyman to clean up rude books.
explanation.walkthrough: PG (paying guest) is only partly retained: P stands outside, G goes inside URATE (CURATE without its head).
explanation.definitionFit: To bowdlerise is to strip offensive passages from a text, which is exactly to expurgate it.

clue.text: Prepares ambush for stories carol singer could tell?

definitions.meaning: to hide ready to attack someone
lies are stories, and a wait is an old word for a carol singer, so lies in a wait

explanation.definitionFit: Lurking out of sight ready to pounce is the idiom for preparing an ambush.

clue.text: Faces twice the traditional 18

parts.note: tradition gives three wise men, so twice the traditional number is six, Roman VI
the answer to 18 down is wise men, and sages are wise men

explanation.surface: A Christmas puzzle line about the faces of the Magi, doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Magi are the traditional wise men: twice three is six (VI), and SAGES stand for 18-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for the face, so visages are faces.

clue.text: Go at more than 1,850 metres per hour overhead

parts.note: to top a speed is to exceed it, going at more than it
a knot is one nautical mile an hour, about 1,852 metres per hour

explanation.surface: Something travelling just over a knot passes overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: A knot is a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile (1,852 m) per hour, so going faster than it is to TOP a KNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft or bun of hair worn on the crown, quite literally overhead.

clue.text: Sweet Cicely's right hand is on my right

indicators.note: in a down or across charade one piece being on another means it comes after it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Cicely has her right hand resting on mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Cicely' looks like a pet name for a woman; it is the herb, also called myrrh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet cicely is an aromatic herb whose common English name is also myrrh.

clue.text: Supplier of "light … on land or sea"?

definitions.text: Supplier of "light … on land or sea"?

parts.words: Supplier of "light … on land or sea"?
parts.note: the quote echoes Wordsworth's 'the light that never was, on sea or land'; the word wanted is the cable or pipe bringing electricity or gas, and also a poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The electricity supply cable brings light, and the same word is an old poetic name for the open ocean.

clue.text: Cross for messer about in boats

definitions.meaning: the Water Rat in The Wind in the Willows says there is nothing like messing about in boats

explanation.definitionFit: Ratty means irritable, and is also the nickname of the Water Rat in Kenneth Grahame's novel.

clue.text: Call to note the thing said in the theatre

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving letters that sound the same but are spelt differently

parts.note: a call is hey, to note is to mark, and the thing is it: hey, mark it

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to have a remark written down during a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Theatre Royal Haymarket is a historic West End playhouse in London; 'Hey, mark it' sounds just like its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Haymarket is a London West End theatre, named after its street.

clue.text: Pupil mimic encompassing his ends

indicators.note: the word for mimic goes round the other letters

parts.note: to ape is to mimic
his refers back to the pupil, whose outer letters are P and L

explanation.surface: A child copies a classmate and surrounds him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to 'Pupil', so its ends are P and L; the definition sense is the apple of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple of the eye is an old name for the pupil.

clue.text: Society man's endeavour to pursue work with clever arguments

indicators.note: the following pieces come after, pursuing, the word for work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
his is the possessive of a man
a try is an endeavour or attempt

explanation.surface: A society gentleman makes an effort to chase work with clever talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is plausible but fallacious reasoning, clever arguments meant to deceive.

clue.text: Reprimand for not very flighty creature, not altogether hot stuff

parts.note: the earwig has wings but seldom flies

indicators.note: the spice word loses its last part, so it is not complete

parts.note: ginger is a hot spice

explanation.surface: Telling off an insect that barely flies for being only partly spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not altogether' trims ER from GINGER, leaving GING. Earwigging is British slang for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwigging is informal British for a talking-to, a reprimand or scolding.

clue.text: Pullman's girl stars in family rave-up

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words for a family party

explanation.surface: Philip Pullman's heroine shines at a lively family party.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyra Belacqua is the heroine of Pullman's His Dark Materials, and Lyra is also a constellation, hence 'stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra is the girl at the centre of His Dark Materials and a northern constellation.

clue.text: Sparky nature to be showing if it's sense

indicators.note: the letters are put on display in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Spirit shows when something makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be showing' signals the anagram of IF IT'S SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feistiness is spirited, lively aggression, the nature of someone sparky.

clue.text: In previous incarnation, what went wrong in Saturday's return for satire on either side of …

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes inside the reversed day
the abbreviation for the day is read backwards

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday

indicators.note: the letters of what are messed up

explanation.surface: Satirical TV once mocked whatever went wrong on Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went wrong' scrambles the word, and 'return' reads the day backwards as TAS. That Was the Week That Was was a 1960s BBC satire show: these words flank 15.
explanation.definitionFit: That was is used after a former name, as in Mrs Smith, Miss Jones that was, meaning formerly.

clue.text: Write to officer (American) that gives name to closest relations

parts.note: to type is to write on a keyboard
Gen is the abbreviation for general, an officer
US means American

explanation.surface: Someone writes to an American officer about naming relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: In biology the type genus is the one that gives its name to its family, the closest grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: A type genus is the genus from which the name of a taxonomic family is derived.

clue.text: … what ends then with explosive piercing 24 king

indicators.note: the explosive goes into the word from 24

parts.note: the answer to 24 down is twee
HE is high explosive
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An explosive is driven into a dainty king.
explanation.walkthrough: Completes the show title from 14: a week is what ends then, i.e. that was the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is a span that closes at a fixed point, so it is what ends then.

clue.text: Half this like this gets setter to reel

parts.note: this clue is number 16, and half of sixteen is eight
so means like this, in this way
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Half of something like this sends the setter reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' means the clue's own number, 16.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: Parson first in seat to see what's coming

indicators.note: the parson and the numeral go inside the seat

parts.note: a pew is a church seat
Rev is short for Reverend, a parson
I is the Roman numeral one, first

explanation.surface: The parson takes the front pew to get a glimpse of what is ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To preview something is to view it in advance, before it arrives.

clue.text: Think-tank, perhaps, with retribution almost up

indicators.note: in a down clue the trimmed word reads upwards
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nemesis is retributive justice

explanation.surface: A think-tank faces retribution that is almost upon it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops S from NEMESIS, and 'up' turns NEMESI to ISEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A think-tank is a body of experts, an example of a group of wise men.

clue.text: Visible intelligence

definitions.meaning: able to be seen, within view

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it means visible; as one word it means deep understanding.

clue.text: Frank's follower to infuriate

definitions.meaning: frankincense: the second half follows frank

explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense splits as frank plus this word, and to incense someone is to make them furious.

clue.text: First for Goliath — part with David's head

indicators.note: only part of the giant's name is used
the first letter of David

explanation.surface: Goliath is first to fall when David takes his head.
explanation.walkthrough: GOL is a part of Goliath; D is David's head. Gold is first place.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is awarded for first place, so it stands for first.

clue.text: Baseline artist?

parts.note: base gives low and line gives the railway abbreviation, naming the Lancashire painter of matchstick figures

explanation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of industrial northern scenes.

clue.text: Two Greek characters reportedly having a go at shrinking?

indicators.note: the two letter names are said, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: the Greek letters psi and chi
taken as written
a go is a try

explanation.surface: Two Greeks have a go at getting smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrinking' looks like getting smaller; a shrink is slang for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, so shrinking is their work.

clue.text: Long time no start

parts.note: a year is a span of time

indicators.note: just the first letter of no

explanation.surface: It is a long time since anything started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' as a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it.

clue.text: Pretty little cloth without a bit of dye

indicators.note: the cloth goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: tweed is a woollen cloth

indicators.note: only the first letter of dye

explanation.surface: Fine fabric that has not been dyed is pretty and small.
explanation.walkthrough: Twee is British for affectedly quaint or dainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for excessively pretty or quaint, cutesy.

clue.text: Wade, say, from Tyneside towards Keswick and Muscat?

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England
Keswick, in the Lake District, lies west-south-west of Newcastle
Muscat is the capital of Oman

explanation.surface: Someone wades from Newcastle to the Lakes and on to Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: Wade is Rebekah Wade, then editor of the Sun; 'Wade' looks like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebekah Wade was a newspaper editor, an example of a female journalist.

clue.text: Virus causing reversion in a part of the ear

indicators.note: the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: the lobe is the soft lower part of the ear

explanation.surface: A virus makes the earlobe go backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebola is a deadly haemorrhagic virus.

clue.text: Way to get over wall, they say

indicators.note: the word is spoken, with a different spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a stile is steps for climbing over a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A path climbs over a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is the step set into a field wall or fence, common on British footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Style means manner, a way of doing something.

clue.text: Entries in order for wine producer

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Records are arranged for a winemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges ENTRIES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nierstein is a German Rhine wine town.
